create_build_hook.description: Create a build hook and return its URL. POSTing to that URL rebuilds and redeploys the site with no credentials, which is how a workflow triggers a Netlify deploy: create the hook once, then call its URL whenever the content it publishes changes. Treat the URL as a secret - anyone who has it can trigger a deploy.
create_build_hook.name: create_build_hook

parameters.description: The site to act on. Pick one, or paste a site ID, a site domain such as my-site.netlify.app, or a Netlify admin URL.
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: What this hook is for, shown in the Netlify UI, such as 'Nightly rebuild'.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: The branch to build. Defaults to the site's production branch.
parameters.name: branch

create_environment_variable.description: Create an environment variable for a team, or for one site when you pick a site. Set which deploy contexts the value applies to. Builds already running do not pick it up - the next deploy does. Scopes and Secret both need a paid Netlify plan; on a free plan leave them empty and Netlify makes the variable readable everywhere.
create_environment_variable.name: create_environment_variable

parameters.description: The team that owns the variable. Netlify keeps environment variables on the team, not on the site.
parameters.name: account_id

parameters.description: The variable's name. Must start with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, numbers and underscores.
parameters.name: key

parameters.description: The value to store.
parameters.name: value

parameters.description: Limit this to one site's own variables. Leave empty to work with the team-wide variables that every site inherits.
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: Which deploys this value applies to. Defaults to all of them.
parameters.name: context

parameters.description: The branch this value applies to. Required when the deploy context is 'One specific branch', and ignored otherwise.
parameters.name: context_parameter

parameters.description: Which parts of the pipeline can read it. Needs a paid Netlify plan - leave empty on a free plan, which gives it all four.
parameters.name: scopes

parameters.description: Hide the value from the Netlify UI, the API and build logs; it cannot be read back afterwards. Needs a paid Netlify plan, because a secret has to have its scopes restricted.
parameters.name: is_secret

create_site.description: Create a Netlify site. The name becomes its netlify.app subdomain and must be unique across all of Netlify; leave it empty to let Netlify invent one. Leave the team empty to create it in the token owner's own team. The site starts with no deploys - link a repository, or use a build hook, to give it one.
create_site.name: create_site

parameters.description: Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, up to 63 characters. Becomes <name>.netlify.app, so it must be free across all of Netlify. Leave empty for a generated name.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: The team to create it in. Leave empty for your own.
parameters.name: account_slug

parameters.description: A domain you already own, to serve the site on.
parameters.name: custom_domain

parameters.description: Require this password to view the site. Leave empty for a public site.
parameters.name: password

parameters.description: Redirect every HTTP request to HTTPS.
parameters.name: force_ssl

parameters.description: The command Netlify runs to build the site, such as 'npm run build'. Leave empty to leave it alone.
parameters.name: build_command

parameters.description: The directory the build writes the finished site into, such as 'dist' or 'build'.
parameters.name: publish_directory

parameters.description: The directory holding the site's serverless functions.
parameters.name: functions_directory

create_site_snippet.description: Inject HTML into this site's pages without redeploying it - an analytics tag, a chat widget, a meta tag. 'Code' goes into every page; 'Thank-you page code' goes only into the page a form submission lands on. Give at least one of the two. The code is injected on the next deploy and on every page served after it.
create_site_snippet.name: create_site_snippet

parameters.description: The site to act on. Pick one, or paste a site ID, a site domain such as my-site.netlify.app, or a Netlify admin URL.
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: What this snippet is for, shown in the Netlify UI.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: HTML to inject into every page, such as a <script> tag. Leave empty to inject only into the thank-you page.
parameters.name: general

parameters.description: Where the code goes in every page. Defaults to the head element.
parameters.name: general_position

parameters.description: HTML to inject only into the page shown after a form is submitted - a conversion tag, typically.
parameters.name: goal

parameters.description: Where the thank-you page code goes. Defaults to the head element.
parameters.name: goal_position

delete_build_hook.description: Delete a build hook. Its URL stops working immediately, so anything still calling it will start failing.
delete_build_hook.name: delete_build_hook

parameters.description: The site to act on. Pick one, or paste a site ID, a site domain such as my-site.netlify.app, or a Netlify admin URL.
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: The build hook to act on, from 'List build hooks'.
parameters.name: build_hook_id

delete_environment_variable.description: Delete an environment variable and every deploy-context value it holds. Builds after this one will not see it, which will break anything that reads it.
delete_environment_variable.name: delete_environment_variable

parameters.description: The team that owns the variable. Netlify keeps environment variables on the team, not on the site.
parameters.name: account_id

parameters.description: The variable's name. Must start with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, numbers and underscores.
parameters.name: key

parameters.description: Limit this to one site's own variables. Leave empty to work with the team-wide variables that every site inherits.
parameters.name: site_id

delete_site.description: Delete a site permanently, along with every deploy, form submission and environment variable belonging to it. This cannot be undone, and the site's netlify.app subdomain becomes available for anyone to claim.
delete_site.name: delete_site

parameters.description: The site to act on. Pick one, or paste a site ID, a site domain such as my-site.netlify.app, or a Netlify admin URL.
parameters.name: site_id

delete_site_snippet.description: Stop injecting a snippet and remove it. The code disappears from the site's pages on the next deploy.
delete_site_snippet.name: delete_site_snippet

parameters.description: The site to act on. Pick one, or paste a site ID, a site domain such as my-site.netlify.app, or a Netlify admin URL.
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: The snippet to act on, from 'List site snippets'.
parameters.name: snippet_id

get_site.description: Read one site in full: its name and URLs, custom domain and domain aliases, team, build command and publish directory, SSL settings, and the deploy currently published on it.
get_site.name: get_site

parameters.description: The site to act on. Pick one, or paste a site ID, a site domain such as my-site.netlify.app, or a Netlify admin URL.
parameters.name: site_id

list_build_hooks.description: List a site's build hooks. Each one carries the URL that triggers a deploy of its branch when something POSTs to it, with no credentials needed.
list_build_hooks.display_str_template: List build hooks for a Netlify site.
list_build_hooks.name: list_build_hooks

parameters.description: The site to act on. Pick one, or paste a site ID, a site domain such as my-site.netlify.app, or a Netlify admin URL.
parameters.name: site_id

list_environment_variables.description: List a team's environment variables, or one site's when you pick a site. Each one reports its value per deploy context, which parts of the pipeline can read it, and who changed it last. A variable marked secret comes back without its value - Netlify never reads a secret back.
list_environment_variables.name: list_environment_variables

parameters.description: The team that owns the variable. Netlify keeps environment variables on the team, not on the site.
parameters.name: account_id

parameters.description: Limit this to one site's own variables. Leave empty to work with the team-wide variables that every site inherits.
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: Only variables set for this deploy context.
parameters.name: context_name

parameters.description: Only variables readable at this point in the pipeline.
parameters.name: scope

list_form_submissions.description: List every submission across all of a site's forms, newest first. Each one carries the submitter's name, email and company where Netlify recognised those fields, and the whole submitted payload under 'data'. Use it to push new form submissions into a CRM or a spreadsheet.
list_form_submissions.name: list_form_submissions

parameters.description: The site to act on. Pick one, or paste a site ID, a site domain such as my-site.netlify.app, or a Netlify admin URL.
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: Which page to read. Defaults to the first.
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: How many to return, 1-100. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: per_page

returns.description: The site's form submissions, newest first

next_page.description: The page to ask for next, or empty at the end

list_site_deploys.description: List a site's deploys, newest first. Each one reports its state ('ready', 'building', 'error' and so on), the branch and commit it came from, its own preview URL, when it was created and published, and the error message if it failed. Read the first one to check whether the latest deploy worked.
list_site_deploys.display_str_template: List deploys for a Netlify site.
list_site_deploys.name: list_site_deploys

parameters.description: The site to act on. Pick one, or paste a site ID, a site domain such as my-site.netlify.app, or a Netlify admin URL.
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: Which page to read. Defaults to the first.
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: How many to return, 1-100. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: per_page

next_page.description: The page to ask for next, or empty at the end

list_site_forms.description: List the forms Netlify detected in this site's deployed HTML, with each form's name, the paths it appears on, the fields it collects and how many submissions it has received. A form only appears here after a deploy that contains it.
list_site_forms.display_str_template: List forms for a Netlify site.
list_site_forms.name: list_site_forms

parameters.description: The site to act on. Pick one, or paste a site ID, a site domain such as my-site.netlify.app, or a Netlify admin URL.
parameters.name: site_id

list_site_snippets.description: List the HTML snippets Netlify injects into this site's pages after each deploy - analytics tags, chat widgets and the like - with the code each one injects and where it goes.
list_site_snippets.display_str_template: List snippets for a Netlify site.
list_site_snippets.name: list_site_snippets

parameters.description: The site to act on. Pick one, or paste a site ID, a site domain such as my-site.netlify.app, or a Netlify admin URL.
parameters.name: site_id

list_sites.description: List the sites the connected Netlify account can see. Returns each site's name, ID, primary and deploy URLs, plan, team, build settings and its currently published deploy. Narrow by name, or to just the sites you own.
list_sites.name: list_sites

parameters.description: Only sites whose name contains this text. Leave empty for all of them.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: Narrow to the sites you own, or were invited to.
parameters.name: filter_by

parameters.description: Which page to read. Defaults to the first.
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: How many to return, 1-100. Defaults to 50.
parameters.name: per_page

next_page.description: The page to ask for next, or empty at the end

set_environment_variable_value.description: Change an existing variable's value for one deploy context, leaving its other contexts alone. The variable must already exist, and you must pick a single context - Netlify does not accept 'all deploy contexts' here. Setting one context on a variable created for all of them splits it into one value per context. The new value takes effect on the next deploy, not on builds already running.
set_environment_variable_value.display_str_template: Set a Netlify environment variable value.
set_environment_variable_value.name: set_environment_variable_value

parameters.description: The team that owns the variable. Netlify keeps environment variables on the team, not on the site.
parameters.name: account_id

parameters.description: The variable's name. Must start with a letter or underscore and contain only letters, numbers and underscores.
parameters.name: key

parameters.description: The value to store.
parameters.name: value

parameters.description: Limit this to one site's own variables. Leave empty to work with the team-wide variables that every site inherits.
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: Which deploys this value applies to. Netlify sets one context at a time here, so pick exactly one - 'all deploy contexts' is only available when the variable is first created.
parameters.name: context

parameters.description: The branch this value applies to. Required when the deploy context is 'One specific branch', and ignored otherwise.
parameters.name: context_parameter

update_build_hook.description: Rename a build hook or point it at a different branch. The hook's URL does not change, so anything already calling it keeps working and starts building the new branch.
update_build_hook.name: update_build_hook

parameters.description: The site to act on. Pick one, or paste a site ID, a site domain such as my-site.netlify.app, or a Netlify admin URL.
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: The build hook to act on, from 'List build hooks'.
parameters.name: build_hook_id

parameters.description: A new name for the hook.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: The branch it should build from now on.
parameters.name: branch

update_site.description: Change a site's settings: rename it, set or clear its custom domain and domain aliases, put it behind a password, change where build notifications go, force HTTPS, or change the build command, publish directory and functions directory. Only the fields you fill in are sent; the rest are left alone. Renaming changes the site's netlify.app subdomain.
update_site.name: update_site

parameters.description: The site to act on. Pick one, or paste a site ID, a site domain such as my-site.netlify.app, or a Netlify admin URL.
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: A new name. Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens; this changes the netlify.app subdomain the site is served on.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: The primary domain to serve the site on.
parameters.name: custom_domain

parameters.description: Other domains that should also serve this site. Replaces the current list.
parameters.name: domain_aliases

parameters.description: Require this password to view the site.
parameters.name: password

parameters.description: Where Netlify sends this site's build notifications.
parameters.name: notification_email

parameters.description: Redirect every HTTP request to HTTPS.
parameters.name: force_ssl

parameters.description: The command Netlify runs to build the site, such as 'npm run build'. Leave empty to leave it alone.
parameters.name: build_command

parameters.description: The directory the build writes the finished site into, such as 'dist' or 'build'.
parameters.name: publish_directory

parameters.description: The directory holding the site's serverless functions.
parameters.name: functions_directory

update_site_snippet.description: Change an injected snippet - its code, where that code goes, or its name. Only the fields you fill in are sent. The change takes effect on the next deploy.
update_site_snippet.name: update_site_snippet

parameters.description: The site to act on. Pick one, or paste a site ID, a site domain such as my-site.netlify.app, or a Netlify admin URL.
parameters.name: site_id

parameters.description: The snippet to act on, from 'List site snippets'.
parameters.name: snippet_id

parameters.description: A new name for the snippet.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: New HTML to inject into every page.
parameters.name: general

parameters.description: Where the code goes in every page. Defaults to the head element.
parameters.name: general_position

parameters.description: New HTML to inject into the form thank-you page.
parameters.name: goal

parameters.description: Where the thank-you page code goes. Defaults to the head element.
parameters.name: goal_position

description: Host and deploy websites on Netlify. Manage sites and their build settings, trigger deploys with build hooks, check whether the latest deploy succeeded, set environment variables, inject snippets, and read form submissions.
